title: Introducing Fact Intelligence
summary: Every fact in your case, traced to its source.
body_markdown:
Every fact in your case, traced to its source.


Litigation turns on facts. Yet establishing them means piecing together evidence scattered across thousands of emails, contracts, transcripts, and witness statements. Accounts conflict, dates are disputed, and a single detail buried in the record can change the case.


Today, we're introducing **Fact Intelligence** , a new way for litigation teams to turn complex case records into connected, source-linked facts. Lawyers can establish what happened, investigate conflicting accounts, and test their position against the evidence.


#### **From documents to facts**


General-purpose AI models struggle with the scale and complexity of litigation evidence. A case record can contain far more information than a model can process at once, so AI typically relies on search and retrieval to select the material relevant to each question. But when facts are scattered across documents, important connections can be missed.


Fact Intelligence takes a different approach. When case documents are uploaded, it processes the evidence before the first question is asked. It extracts reported facts, identifies the people and dates involved, and connects related information across documents, preserving links to the original sources.


This creates a structured factual record that the Legora Agent can investigate. Rather than reconstructing the context from scratch with every question, the Agent can work from connected facts across the evidence, helping lawyers explore relationships, investigate inconsistencies, and verify findings against the source material.


#### **Investigate the facts, build the case**


With the facts connected across the record, lawyers can investigate questions that would otherwise require extensive manual review.


**Build chronologies of what happened and when.** Bring events together across documents, with each entry linked to its source. Trace how events unfolded, identify disputed dates, and establish a clearer sequence of events.


**Establish who knew what, and when** . Follow people, events, and communications across the record to understand when information was shared, who was involved, and how accounts developed over time.


**Uncover conflicting accounts.** Surface inconsistencies between witness statements, emails, and other evidence. Examine competing versions of events side by side, with the original sources available to verify each finding.


**Test your position against the evidence.** Investigate the facts that support an argument and those that could undermine it. Examine whether a witness statement or draft pleading holds against the record, and identify the points that need closer scrutiny.


Instead of manually piecing together the story, lawyers can spend more time interpreting the evidence, assessing its implications, and deciding how to build the strongest case.


#### **From facts to argument**


Understanding the facts is only the beginning. The real value comes from putting them to work.


By bringing Fact Intelligence together with Legal Research, lawyers can assess how the law applies to the specific facts of their case. That same factual understanding can inform statements of facts, briefs, witness preparation, and case strategy, with the evidence behind each finding available for review.


We're building toward a more connected litigation experience in Legora, where lawyers can move from investigating the evidence to applying the law and developing their arguments in one place.
